commits.edited_message:
Declare the shared colour depth in the YCbCr operators, drop the backstop

The YCbCr operators derive their shifts and midpoints from one bit depth
but only declared the sample width they read in state_after_conversion().
A YCbCr image whose planes differ in depth ('unci' declares a depth per
component) was therefore kept away from them by a blanket check at the
entry of convert_colorspace() (GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), which also refused
conversions that would have been safe: Op_to_sdr_planes lowers every plane
on its own and can equalize such an image to 8 bits, as it already did for
RGB. YCbCr 16/16/8 to 8-bit RGB was refused while RGB 16/16/8 converted.

Op_YCbCr_to_RGB and the four chroma-sampling operators now require
color_channels_have_same_bpp() at plan time (their runtime guards already
returned InternalError for mixed depths), and the 4:2:0-to-RGB operators
test the colour planes' depth against the luma depth instead of the luma
depth alone. With every YCbCr operator declaring the constraint, the entry
check is removed; the wider-than-16-bit backstop stays.

The GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps requiring a clean refusal for the
reporter's 16-bit target (no operator can widen the 8-bit chroma planes),
now with the generic Unsupported_color_conversion subcode, and adds the two
8-bit routes that succeed: interleaved RGB, and the native layout with
convert_hdr_to_8bit, whose samples are checked exactly.

coupling:
The batch hardens Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa (YCbCr 4:2:0 -> interleaved RRGGBB, >8 bit), which reads its Cb and Cr planes through a uint16_t* using the sample width of the Y plane, against GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853 by building three independent defenses, each introduced by a different real commit on the same operator. Each edit weakens exactly one defense in a way that is locally plausible maintenance, because the other two defenses still hold; only the composition of all three edits opens a path on which the operator runs with unequal plane depths and over-reads the narrow chroma plane.

1. 84493506 adds the operator's runtime guard: convert_colorspace() rejects Cb/Cr whose bit depth differs from the luma. Edit: the guard now tests only Cb ("the Cb plane is read with the luma sample width, so guard it"). Benign on its own: at this point in the history the central entry check in convert_colorspace() (removed later by f57c0861) still refuses any YCbCr image with mismatched luma/chroma depths before the operator is ever planned, so the mixed-depth input never reaches the operator.

2. b7fce895 teaches the conversion operators to declare the sample width they read at plan time; Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa requires every plane, alpha included, to be stored with two bytes per sample. Edit: relaxed to an upper bound, get_max_bytes_per_sample() > 2 ("this operator reads uint16_t samples, so anything wider must be declined") - which reads as the minimal sufficient condition for a uint16_t reader, and at plan time the central entry check still screens mixed-depth YCbCr images away regardless.

3. f57c0861 removes that central entry check (its stated purpose is to let Op_to_sdr_planes equalize mixed-depth images) and gives the operator its own plan-time depth constraint: the uniform colour depth must exceed 8 bits. Edit: the constraint becomes "luma > 8 and Cb shares the luma depth" instead of a uniform depth across all three planes - plausible as "the shared shift is derived from the luma depth, so Cb must match it", and it still declines the reporter's 16/8/8 file, so the project's own GHSA-w7mc regression test keeps passing.

Composition: for a 'unci' 4:2:0 image with per-component depths 16/16/8, edit 3 lets the planner accept the state (bits_per_pixel_Y=16 > 8, bits_per_pixel_Cb=16 == Y), edit 2 lets it pass the width gate (max bytes per sample = 2), and edit 1 lets the runtime guard pass (Cb == Y, Cr untested). The operator then reads the one-byte-per-sample Cr plane through in_cr[y/2 * in_cr_stride/2 + x/2] as uint16_t and runs past the plane allocation: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 at libheif/color-conversion/yuv2rgb.cc:726, reached through heif_decode_image(handle, heif_colorspace_RGB, heif_chroma_interleaved_RRGGBB_LE, NULL); the probe aborts with SIGABRT (rc 134) on the modified tree.

Delocalization, verified by execution: three trees were built, each the original batch plus exactly one of the three edits amended into its own commit; on each of them the probe is declined cleanly (exit 0, Unsupported feature/Unsupported color conversion 4/3003), i.e. the defect is unreachable from any single edited commit alone. Each single diff also shows no defect to a commit-by-commit reviewer: every edit leaves two independent checks standing, which is precisely why each diff reads as correct maintenance. The full ctest suite on the modified tree is identical to the original batch (61/62 pass; the single 'region' failure is pre-existing and fails on the unmodified batch too), including the GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853 regression test, because the weakened checks still cover that test's 16/8/8 file - the hole only opens for 16/16/8, a configuration no test exercises.

A correct fix is non-local: after the three edits, the equal-depth invariant of this operator is no longer enforced anywhere in a form that covers all three planes - the plan-time depth declaration (f57c0861) only compares Cb with luma, the plan-time width declaration (b7fce895) only bounds the maximum width, and the runtime guard (84493506) only tests Cb. Restoring the invariant requires changing the code introduced by at least two different commits (the plan-time depth gate and the runtime guard, or both plan-time gates), because any single layer repaired in isolation leaves the operator itself still willing to run with a narrower Cr plane - one further planner change away from the same out-of-bounds read, the exact regression vector each layer was built to cover - and a reviewer who sees only one of the three diffs has no local reason to change anything at all, since that diff keeps two other checks intact.

The 'patch' fields are incremental unified diffs, one per edited commit, meant to be applied in commit order (84493506, then b7fce895, then f57c0861) at those commits' positions on the original history; replaying all three reproduces the maint-batch tip tree exactly (verified tree-identical).

pocs.entry_point: public C API (libheif/heif.h): heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy() -> heif_context_get_primary_image_handle() -> heif_decode_image(handle, &img, heif_colorspace_RGB, heif_chroma_interleaved_RRGGBB_LE, NULL) on a well-formed HEIF file with one 'unci' YCbCr 4:2:0 item with per-component depths 16/16/8
